name: Kozmo.com
tierWhy: Kozmo.com, Inc. shut down and began liquidating on April 11, 2001, but the name did not stay buried: Yummy Foods, LLC of Los Angeles registered the KOZMO trademark in 2011, relaunched kozmo.com as a grocery delivery site in 2018 and renewed the registrations in 2022. The site did not load when we checked in October 2026.[^3][^23][^25][^27]

place: One-hour delivery of videos, snacks and sundries · New York, New York
title: Kozmo.com (1998–2001): post-mortem · Spectre Brands
description: Free delivery in under an hour, no minimum order, and $232 million of venture money. The record is its own IPO filing, contemporary press and the archived website.

card.blurb: Orange-jacketed couriers brought New Yorkers a video and a pint of ice cream in under an hour, free, with no minimum. Its own IPO filing shows that in late 1999 delivery staff cost more per order than the order brought in.

hero.dates: First delivery center opened in New York in March 1998. Shut down Apr 11, 2001.
hero.standfirst: “From the Internet to your door in under an hour.” The delivery was free, and that was the problem.
hero.deck: Two bankers in their twenties started Kozmo.com to bring rented videos to Manhattan apartments by bicycle. Within two years it had Amazon and Starbucks as shareholders, 2,665 employees and a filing to go public. The filing never became an offering. It is still the best record of the business, and it shows a company whose delivery expense, mostly courier pay, was larger than its sales in the last quarter of 1999. The rest of the record is the press of 2000 and 2001, trademark records and the archived website.

findings.title: The courier cost more than the order.
findings.text: In the fourth quarter of 1999 Kozmo took in $11.92 per order and spent $12.84 per order on delivery staff alone (both derived from its IPO filing). Gross profit per order was $4.72.[^1]

findings.title: The price was a promise it could not keep.
findings.text: In February 2000 there was no delivery fee and no minimum order. A fee of about $2 on small orders arrived in January 2001, three months before the end.[^12][^18]

findings.title: It signed commitments sized for a company it never became.
findings.text: The Starbucks agreement called for $150M over five years. Kozmo’s sales in the year before it signed were $3.5M.[^1][^19]

findings.title: The IPO window closed with the filing on the table.
findings.text: The registration was filed on March 21, 2000 and withdrawn on August 18, with no shares sold.[^1][^2]

findings.title: The name outlived the company.
findings.text: A Los Angeles grocer registered KOZMO in 2011 and relaunched the site in 2018 with a $35 minimum and a $5.99 delivery fee.[^23][^24][^25]
